veranderings.blok: Tselane en die stem by die deur
veranderings.voor: sy bly by die ou hut agter
veranderings.na: sy bly agter by die ou hut
veranderings.rede: Keeping the separable 'bly agter' together reads more naturally for a Grade 4 learner.

veranderings.blok: Tselane en die stem by die deur
veranderings.na: Tselane maak die deur net oop as
veranderings.rede: 'Oopmaak' without an object is loose; naming the door, already in the block, makes the sentence clear.

veranderings.voor: Toe kom die hoofman self, 'n slang met vyf koppe, nader.
veranderings.na: Toe kom die hoofman self nader, 'n slang met vyf koppe.
veranderings.rede: The apposition splits the separable verb 'nader kom' and leaves 'nader' stranded at the end.
'Gelos' is colloquial; 'agtergelaat' is the standard written form with the same meaning.
'Iemand sien aankom' is the natural Afrikaans for seeing someone approach.
'Agternasleep' is a compound separable verb, so the past participle is written as one word (like agternaloop).

vlae.teks: Hy word 'n man, en hy hou die meeste van haar.
vlae.rede: 'Die meeste' has no comparison stated, so it is unclear whether he likes her more than her sister or more than anything; fixing it would mean guessing the intended content.
